summary.headline: Eveready Q2 FY27 revenue rose 10.7% YoY to INR 428.2 crores and EBITDA grew 8.9% to INR 53.8 crores, with margin at 12.6%.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 marked the eighth consecutive quarter of YoY revenue growth, with PAT of INR 31.9 crores against a loss of INR 7.9 crores last year (which included a INR 37.7 crore exceptional loss). Management said operating margin contracted about 20 bps, driven by elevated material costs (zinc up 36% YoY on average) and channel and product mix, partly offset by calibrated price increases and cost control. Jammu alkaline battery plant was commissioned in May and billing started in September, with output still largely from imported stock. Net debt was INR 153 crores as of September, before the INR 90 crores received from the second Noida plot sale in October. Management expects H2 to be more difficult than H1 as commodity prices harden.

segments.name: Batteries - Alkaline
segments.commentary: Volume grew 30% YoY in Q2 FY27 and market share rose versus last year; management says alkaline gains are coming from within dry cells, not yet from Panasonic. Jammu plant output is to become fully indigenous from this quarter.

segments.name: Batteries - Carbon zinc
segments.commentary: Described as stable with growth despite elevated raw material costs, maintained through calibrated pricing and cost management.

segments.name: Flashlights
segments.commentary: Rechargeable flashlights grew 33.2% YoY, more than offsetting a decline in conventional battery-operated flashlights; new SHOR rechargeable with animal alarm launched.

segments.name: Lighting
segments.commentary: Emergency LED bulbs grew 26% YoY; Xtrabright launched (claimed up to 2x brighter in outages). Lighting overall near breakeven in H1; about 85% of lighting is B2C and reported EBITDA positive, while professional lighting is loss-making.

segments.name: Mosquito products and electrical accessories
segments.commentary: Portable liquid vaporiser launched (patent applied); Mosquito Racquet is a leading organised player within 3 years. Electrical accessories, insulated tapes, wires and MCBs are gaining momentum.

capex_capacity: Jammu alkaline battery plant: commercial production from May 2026, ramping gradually; billing began September 2026 after ageing of 28-42 days and imported stock depletion. Management expects improved utilisation in coming quarters.
Local manufacturing expected to deliver at least 6-7% better accrual than imports on current variables; 12-13% under stable conditions.

Jammu capex about INR 200 crores; capital subsidy under NCSS registration not yet granted, so no accrual booked. If received, management estimates INR 20-25 crores annually for 10 years, subject to a cap (example INR 250 crores approved implies about INR 25 crores a year).
Second Noida plot sale closed on 13 October 2026; INR 90 crores received. Management indicated one or two more plants could be realigned after Jammu settles, with no firm decision.
No major capex currently planned; management says the company could be debt-free within about two years, possibly sooner.
demand_pricing: Uneven monsoon weighed on rural demand; zinc and other input costs remained elevated. Management says commodity prices are hardening rather than softening, so H2 will be harder than H1.
Price increases taken across lighting and batteries; management says pricing erosion in LED has softened and that longer-tail categories (electrical accessories, wires, MCBs) have resisted erosion.

Alkaline batteries priced about 2x zinc carbon currently, potentially 2.5x at steady state. Alkaline is about 10% of revenue? Not stated; B2B (OEM/institutional, incl. private label) is about 10% of total revenue.
Advertising and sales promotion held at 10-10.5% of revenue; no cut to fund margins.
E-commerce and quick commerce grew over 50% YoY in Q2.
Dry cell volumes flat as alkaline cannibalises zinc; value growing. Dry cell penetration about 85-90%.
EPR for dry cell batteries: pricing ambiguity and compliance still under discussion with MoEFCC and CPCB; FY25-FY26 compliance deadline extended to 30 November; management expects clarity by Q3.
guidance_outlook: Management expects to recover most material-cost pressure in Q3 but full recovery likely only in Q4, given several price corrections taken.
H2 FY27 expected to be more challenging than H1; management aims to sustain consistent results (targeting 9th and 10th consecutive quarters of growth).
Medium-term projections (CAGR for battery, non-battery and new categories) to be shared around February-March 2027.
Mosquito portfolio (rackets and liquid vaporisers) could cross INR 100 crores by end FY29; liquid vaporiser market about INR 2,800 crores with a target 3-4% share.
Net debt could reach zero within about two years, possibly earlier given INR 90 crores proceeds.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the margin compression and how will margins play out?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said operating margin fell about 20 bps on elevated material costs and channel and product mix, offset by calibrated pricing and other-cost control; recovery expected in Q3 and full recovery in Q4.

qa_highlights.question: When will Jammu contribute to revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Commercial production began May 2026 and billing started September; imported stock supplied most alkaline sales in Q2 (not more than 10% from Jammu), with Jammu expected to be largely the source from Q3.

qa_highlights.question: Net debt trajectory over the next two years?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said no major capex is planned and the company should be debt-free within about two years, possibly sooner; INR 90 crores Noida proceeds were largely used to reduce debt.

qa_highlights.question: Panasonic supply disruption and share gains in dry cells?
qa_highlights.answer: CEO said share gains are so far coming from alkaline, not Panasonic; any shift would show from October to December as dry cell players' 40-45 day channel stock runs down.

qa_highlights.question: Jammu capital subsidy and its size?
qa_highlights.answer: Subsidy under NCSS registration not yet granted due to state fund shortage; if approved, could be INR 20-25 crores a year for 10 years, subject to a cap.

qa_highlights.question: Size of new product revenue and mosquito opportunity?
qa_highlights.answer: Half of H1 growth came from core categories and half from products launched in the last 24 months (excluding alkaline); mosquito rackets and liquid vaporisers could cross INR 100 crores by end FY29.

risks_watch: Zinc and other commodity costs are hardening; H2 margin recovery depends on pricing pass-through and efficiency.
EPR for dry cell batteries: pricing mechanism ambiguity and compliance deadline of 30 November 2026; financial impact not yet provided for.
Jammu capital subsidy not yet approved; no accrual booked and funding delays at the state/DPIIT level.
Jammu ramp-up and vendor localisation; alkaline is still a small share of dry cell sales.
Professional lighting remains loss-making; full-year lighting breakeven depends on its turnaround.
Management declined to give a multi-year CAGR; a projection is expected around February-March 2027.
Further plant rationalisation and capital recycling possible but not confirmed.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand and the alkaline and rechargeable trajectory, but cautious on the near term: management says H2 will be harder than H1 as commodity prices harden. Evasive on EPR impact, subsidy timing and multi-year growth targets, deferring these to the next quarter or to February-March 2027.
key_quotes: Commodity prices are not softening, they're hardening. Will H2 be very easy? No, it's going to be more difficult than H1.

It is the volumes that are a bit sluggish. Also, for a category whose penetration would be close to 85% to 90% in India, given that you know, a lot are there across the country everywhere, it's a merely highly mature category.
You can fairly assume in the next 2 years, we should be definitely a debt-free company, unless any decisions taken otherwise.

growth.why: Q2 FY27 revenue +10.7% and EBITDA +8.9% YoY, with management guiding H2 harder than H1 on hardening commodities and only partial margin recovery in Q3; Jammu plant is commissioned but ramping with no numeric utilisation or volume target, and no explicit revenue growth guidance was given.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Operating margin fell ~20 bps to 12.6% on zinc up 36% YoY; management expects most material-cost pressure recovered in Q3 but full recovery only in Q4, and says H2 will be harder than H1.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Jammu alkaline plant already commissioned (May 2026) and billing from September; imported stock is being replaced by Jammu output from Q3, so the capacity is coming live rather than new, with ramp-up still gradual.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Alkaline volume grew 30% YoY in Q2, rechargeable flashlights +33.2%, emergency LED +26%, and e-commerce +50%; but dry cell volumes are flat and rural demand was hit by uneven monsoon.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Management says no major capex is planned and Jammu (~INR 200 crore) is settling; one or two more plant realignments are possible with no firm decision, so a new capex announcement is conditional.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management guided H2 harder than H1 with commodity prices hardening, and gave no numeric revenue or margin upgrade; the 9th and 10th consecutive quarters of growth are the stated aim, not a raise.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Margin recovery is only partial in Q3 and full recovery may slip to Q4 or later, with zinc up 36% YoY; EPR compliance cost is not yet quantified.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Portable liquid vaporiser (patent applied), SHOR rechargeable with animal alarm and Xtrabright were launched in Q2; management targets Mosquito portfolio above INR 100 crore by end FY29.

rows.label: Debt-free within about 2 years
rows.why: Net debt INR 153 crore at September before INR 90 crore Noida plot proceeds in October; CFO says no major capex is planned and the company should be debt-free in about 2 years, possibly sooner.

rows.label: EPR dry cell clarity and subsidy decision
rows.why: EPR compliance deadline extended to 30 November and clarity expected by Q3, with financial impact not yet provided; Jammu NCSS subsidy (INR 20-25 crore a year if approved) not yet granted.

rows.label: Medium-term CAGR disclosure
rows.why: Battery, non-battery and new-category CAGR projections are to be shared around February-March 2027; management declined a multi-year CAGR on this call.

tone.note: Management was confident on alkaline, rechargeables and the Mosquito portfolio, but cautious on H2 margins as zinc hardens; analysts pressed on margin recovery, EPR, Jammu subsidy and multi-year growth, which management largely deferred to Feb-Mar 2027.
